For the first milestone, the worker logic remains in-process inside the web app API layer.
1. User submits YouTube URL or concept query.
2. if that fails, inspect subtitles and automatic captions via `yt-dlp`
3. if captions are missing or poor quality, fetch audio via `yt-dlp`
4. upload audio to Gemini Files API
5. transcribe or summarize audio with Gemini audio understanding
- add Google Cloud Speech-to-Text only if you later need stricter dedicated transcription behavior
- If you truly want audio-first processing instead of captions-first, the system can do that, but cost and latency will increase.
- For MVP, caption-first with transcription fallback is the better default unless you have a strong reason to ignore available captions.
- A dedicated transcript endpoint is useful even before the full report pipeline because it lets you debug video coverage and quality separately.
2. server calls Gemini with `google_search` grounding enabled
3. model returns a grounded draft plus search metadata
4. app runs a second Gemini call to normalize that grounded draft into report JSON
- Gemini supports grounding with Google Search.
- Gemini supports structured outputs with schemas.
- worker handles transcript extraction, Gemini calls, and export generation
- Gemini responses are stored as normalized JSON in PostgreSQL
- YouTube ingestion and PDF generation already require backend work
That makes a long-lived container platform a better first deployment target.
- set up TypeScript, Tailwind, Prisma, PostgreSQL
- generate Korean report draft with Gemini structured output
- Speech-to-text / audio understanding: Gemini Files API + audio understanding
2. complete YouTube URL to summary flow
- YouTube download and transcript handling must respect platform policies and copyright boundaries.
- transcript quality directly affects summary quality
